```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Yao et al. (2026) characterised the pharmacokinetics of SIG001, a humanized
monoclonal antibody against tumour-associated sialylated IgG (SIA-IgG), in
cynomolgus monkeys and CD-1 mice, and projected human PK by allometric scaling
of the monkey model to choose a first-in-human (FIH) dose and a
pharmacologically active dose (PAD) range. The paper contributes three models,
all two-compartment with linear elimination:

| Model | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Yao_2026_SIG001_cyno` | Population PK fit to cynomolgus monkeys (Table 1) |
| `Yao_2026_SIG001_mouse` | Population PK fit to CD-1 mice (Table 2) |
| `Yao_2026_SIG001_human` | Allometric human projection from the monkey fit (Equation 1, Results) |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yao_2026_SIG001_cyno"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2026.1904283>

All three models carry body-weight-normalised parameters (L/kg, L/h/kg), as the
paper reports them (mL/kg, mL/h/kg). Doses are given in mg/kg to a nominal
1-kg subject, and `Cc` is returned in ug/mL (mg/L).

# Population

**Cynomolgus monkey.** 18 healthy animals in three single-IV-dose groups (5,
15 and 30 mg/kg; 3 male and 3 female per group), mean body weight 2.24 kg,
serially sampled from 0.5 h to 28 days (251 quantifiable and 1 BQL ELISA
observations, LLOQ 100 ng/mL).

**Mouse.** Non-tumour-bearing CD-1 mice given single IV doses of 5, 10 or
20 mg/kg. Each mouse gave two samples, six mice per time point per dose
(twelve at 28 days), sexes balanced: about 45 mice per dose group, 216
quantifiable and 54 BQL observations. BQL data were handled with the M3 method,
and only IIV on CL was estimable.

**Human.** No human data. Parameters are the monkey estimates scaled to a
70-kg adult (Equation 1); the 30% IIV on CL and 10% proportional residual
error are the authors' assumed values for monoclonal antibodies.

```{r population}
for (m in c("Yao_2026_SIG001_cyno", "Yao_2026_SIG001_mouse",
            "Yao_2026_SIG001_human")) {
  pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))$population
  cat(m, ": ", pop$species, "; n = ", pop$n_subjects, "; ",
      pop$dose_range, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure (all species) | 2-cmt, linear CL, IV bolus | Methods 'Development and evaluation of population PK model'; Results |
| Monkey CL, VC, Q, VP | 0.386 mL/h/kg, 47.2 mL/kg, 1.05 mL/h/kg, 31.4 mL/kg | Table 1 |
| Monkey IIV CL, IIV VC | 18.8%, 16.2% | Table 1 |
| Monkey proportional error | 12.6% | Table 1 |
| Mouse CL, VC, Q, VP | 1.37 mL/h/kg, 57.7 mL/kg, 3.48 mL/h/kg, 32.9 mL/kg | Table 2 |
| Mouse IIV CL | 43.4% | Table 2 |
| Mouse proportional error | 20.6% | Table 2 |
| Allometric equation, exponents | 0.8 (CL), 0.75 (Q), 1.0 (VC), 0.95 (VP); 70 kg vs 2.24 kg | Equation 1 and following text |
| Human CL, VC, Q, VP | 0.194 mL/h/kg, 47.2 mL/kg, 0.44 mL/h/kg, 26.4 mL/kg | Results, 'Projection of FIH dose of SIG001' |
| Human IIV CL (assumed) | 30% | Results; Discussion |
| Human proportional error (assumed) | 10% | Results; Discussion |
| Validation targets | NCA t1/2 153 h (monkey), 64.7 h (mouse); human t1/2 ~11 days; median Cmax,ss 45 ug/mL at 1.5 mg/kg Q2W; all 1.0 mg/kg Q2W predictions < 50 ug/mL; PAD 1.8-7.0 mg/kg Q2W | Results; Figure 5 |

The human values printed in Results are reproduced by Equation 1 from the
monkey estimates:

```{r allometry-check}
bw_ratio <- 70 / 2.24
monkey <- c(cl = 0.386, vc = 47.2, q = 1.05, vp = 31.4)
alpha <- c(cl = 0.8, vc = 1.0, q = 0.75, vp = 0.95)
# Absolute scaling, then back to per kg: P_kg,human = P_kg,monkey * ratio^(alpha - 1)
scaled <- monkey * bw_ratio^(alpha - 1)
printed <- c(cl = 0.194, vc = 47.2, q = 0.44, vp = 26.4)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(parameter = names(scaled), monkey = monkey,
             equation_1 = signif(scaled, 3), printed = printed) |>
    dplyr::rename("Parameter" = parameter, "Monkey (Table 1)" = monkey,
                  "Equation 1" = equation_1, "Printed human value" = printed),
  caption = "Human per-kg parameters: Equation 1 vs the values printed in Results (mL/h/kg or mL/kg)."
)
stopifnot(all(abs(scaled / printed - 1) < 0.01))
```

# Shared helpers

```{r helpers}
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, seq(12, 672, by = 12))))

single_dose_events <- function(doses, n_per_dose, grid) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), function(i) {
    ids <- (i - 1L) * n_per_dose + seq_len(n_per_dose)
    dose_rows <- data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = doses[[i]],
                            cmt = "central")
    obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = grid)
    obs_rows$evid <- 0L
    obs_rows$amt <- 0
    obs_rows$cmt <- "central"
    out <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows)
    out$treatment <- paste(doses[[i]], "mg/kg")
    out
  })) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

run_single_dose_nca <- function(sim, events) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
  dose <- events |>
    dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
                               concu = "ug/mL", timeu = "h")
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                               doseu = "mg/kg")
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE,
                          aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}

vpc_summary <- function(sim) {
  # The bolus is ordered before the time-0 observation, so every time-0
  # concentration is the post-dose dose / VC and plots on a log axis.
  sim |>
    dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

# Cynomolgus monkey (Table 1 model)

```{r cyno-sim}
mod_cyno <- readModelDb("Yao_2026_SIG001_cyno")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261)
ev_cyno <- single_dose_events(c(5, 15, 30), n_per_dose = 100, grid = obs_grid)
sim_cyno <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cyno, events = ev_cyno, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r cyno-vpc, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Yao 2026: simulated median and 90% prediction interval of SIG001 serum concentration after single IV doses in cynomolgus monkeys (100 simulated animals per dose)."}
vpc_summary(sim_cyno) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "SIG001 (ug/mL)")
```

```{r cyno-nca}
nca_cyno <- run_single_dose_nca(sim_cyno, ev_cyno)
knitr::kable(summary(nca_cyno), caption = "PKNCA summary, simulated monkeys.")
```

# Mouse (Table 2 model)

```{r mouse-sim}
mod_mouse <- readModelDb("Yao_2026_SIG001_mouse")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20262)
ev_mouse <- single_dose_events(c(5, 10, 20), n_per_dose = 100, grid = obs_grid)
sim_mouse <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse, events = ev_mouse, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r mouse-vpc, fig.cap = "Replicates the upper panels of Figure 3 of Yao 2026: simulated median and 90% prediction interval of SIG001 serum concentration after single IV doses in CD-1 mice (100 simulated mice per dose). The dashed line is the ELISA LLOQ of 0.1 ug/mL."}
vpc_summary(sim_mouse) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "darkorange", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "darkorange4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.1, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "SIG001 (ug/mL)")
```

```{r mouse-nca}
nca_mouse <- run_single_dose_nca(sim_mouse, ev_mouse)
knitr::kable(summary(nca_mouse), caption = "PKNCA summary, simulated mice.")
```

## Comparison against the published NCA half-lives

Yao 2026 reports one NCA half-life per species ("153 h in cynomolgus monkeys and
64.7 h in mice", Results), without a dose group. Each published value is
therefore compared against every simulated dose group; the model is linear, so
the simulated half-life does not depend on dose.

```{r nca-compare}
published_cyno <- tibble::tibble(treatment = c("5 mg/kg", "15 mg/kg", "30 mg/kg"),
                                 half.life = 153)
published_mouse <- tibble::tibble(treatment = c("5 mg/kg", "10 mg/kg", "20 mg/kg"),
                                  half.life = 64.7)
cmp_cyno <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_cyno, reference = published_cyno, by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp_mouse <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_mouse, reference = published_mouse, by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    dplyr::mutate(cmp_cyno, Species = "cynomolgus monkey", .before = 1),
    dplyr::mutate(cmp_mouse, Species = "mouse", .before = 1)
  ),
  caption = "Simulated (median of 100 animals per dose) vs published NCA half-life. * marks a difference above 20%."
)

hl <- as.data.frame(nca_cyno$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life")
hl_mouse <- as.data.frame(nca_mouse$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life")
stopifnot(
  abs(median(hl$PPORRES) / 153 - 1) < 0.15,
  # The mouse model's terminal half-life sits below the published NCA value
  # (see the narrative); this only guards against a gross transcription error.
  abs(median(hl_mouse$PPORRES) / 64.7 - 1) < 0.40
)
```

The monkey half-life agrees with the published NCA value. The mouse model's
terminal half-life (about 48 h for the typical animal) is roughly 25% shorter
than the 64.7 h NCA value. The published value is a naive-pooled NCA of sparse
data in which 20% of samples, concentrated at the late time points, were BQL
and so absent from the terminal fit, while the model was fit with the M3 method
that uses those BQL records; the paper itself notes the conditional weighted
residuals drift upwards towards 28 days. The parameters were not adjusted.

# Human projection (Equation 1 model)

## First-in-human safety projection (Figure 5)

```{r human-sim}
mod_human <- readModelDb("Yao_2026_SIG001_human")
tau <- 14 * 24
dose_times <- seq(0, 10 * 7 * 24, by = tau)
human_grid <- seq(0, 12 * 7 * 24, by = 4)

human_events <- function(dose, n, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = dose_times)
  dose_rows$evid <- 1L
  dose_rows$amt <- dose
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = human_grid)
  obs_rows$evid <- 0L
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  out <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows)
  out$cmt <- "central"
  out$treatment <- sprintf("%.1f mg/kg Q2W", dose)
  dplyr::arrange(out, id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

ev_human <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  human_events(1.0, 200, 0L),
  human_events(1.5, 200, 200L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_human[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20263)
sim_human <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_human, events = ev_human, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r human-fig5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Yao 2026: simulated SIG001 serum concentration in humans at (A) 1.0 mg/kg and (B) 1.5 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks; solid line = median, band = 90% prediction interval including residual error (200 simulated subjects per regimen). Dashed line: the 50 ug/mL cytokine-release threshold."}
sim_human |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim),
                   p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / (7 * 24), p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "seagreen", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "seagreen4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "SIG001 (ug/mL)")
```

PKNCA over the last dosing interval (weeks 10-12) gives the steady-state peak:

```{r human-nca}
conc_h <- sim_human |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_h <- ev_human |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
nca_human <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_h, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "ug/mL", timeu = "h"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_h, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg/kg"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = max(dose_times), end = max(dose_times) + tau,
                         cmax = TRUE, cav = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
knitr::kable(summary(nca_human), caption = "PKNCA summary over the 6th dosing interval (weeks 10-12).")

cmax_ss <- as.data.frame(nca_human$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax")
cmax_med_15 <- median(cmax_ss$PPORRES[cmax_ss$treatment == "1.5 mg/kg Q2W"])

# Peak with residual error, the quantity the paper's prediction interval shows.
peak_sim <- sim_human |>
  dplyr::filter(time == max(dose_times)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(peak_sim |>
               dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Median peak (ug/mL)" = p50,
                             "95th percentile peak (ug/mL)" = p95),
             digits = 1,
             caption = "Simulated peak after the 6th dose, including residual error.")
p95_10 <- peak_sim$p95[peak_sim$treatment == "1.0 mg/kg Q2W"]
stopifnot(
  length(cmax_med_15) == 1L, !is.na(cmax_med_15), length(p95_10) == 1L,
  # Results: 'the median of predicted Cmax,ss for the 1.5 mg/kg dose regimen was 45 ug/mL'
  abs(cmax_med_15 / 45 - 1) < 0.10,
  # Results: 'the predictions for the 1.0 mg/kg dose regimen were all below the 50 ug/mL threshold'
  p95_10 < 50
)
```

The median steady-state Cmax at 1.5 mg/kg Q2W is
`r sprintf("%.1f", cmax_med_15)` ug/mL (paper: 45 ug/mL), and the upper
prediction bound at 1.0 mg/kg Q2W stays below 50 ug/mL, matching the paper's
choice of 1.5 mg/kg / 10 = 0.15 mg/kg Q2W as the FIH dose.

## Human half-life

```{r human-halflife}
p <- c(cl = 0.194, vc = 47.2, q = 0.44, vp = 26.4) # mL/h/kg, mL/kg
k10 <- p[["cl"]] / p[["vc"]]
k12 <- p[["q"]] / p[["vc"]]
k21 <- p[["q"]] / p[["vp"]]
s <- k10 + k12 + k21
beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
t_half_days <- log(2) / beta / 24
cat(sprintf("Typical human terminal half-life = %.1f days\n", t_half_days))
stopifnot(abs(t_half_days / 11 - 1) < 0.10)
```

The paper states "approximately 11 days".

## Pharmacologically active dose (PAD) projection

The paper matches the steady-state average concentration (Cavg,ss = AUCss /
tau) of the efficacious mouse regimens (2.5 and 10 mg/kg) to human Q2W
regimens and reports a human PAD of 1.8-7.0 mg/kg Q2W. For a linear model
Cavg,ss = dose / (CL x tau), so the human Cavg,ss at the PAD bounds and the
mouse Cavg,ss at the xenograft doses can be computed directly from the typical
values. The mouse dosing interval used for this step is not stated; the
xenograft schedules in Supplementary Table S1 were every 3 to 4 days, and the
Discussion's statement that 50 ug/mL is the Cavg of 5 mg/kg in mice implies an
interval of about 3 days.

```{r pad}
cl_mouse <- 1.37 / 1000 # L/h/kg
cl_human <- 0.194 / 1000
pad <- tibble::tibble(
  mouse_dose = c(2.5, 10),
  mouse_cavg_q3d = mouse_dose / (cl_mouse * 72),
  mouse_cavg_q4d = mouse_dose / (cl_mouse * 96),
  human_pad = c(1.8, 7.0),
  human_cavg_q2w = human_pad / (cl_human * tau)
)
knitr::kable(
  pad |>
    dplyr::rename("Mouse dose (mg/kg)" = mouse_dose,
                  "Mouse Cavg,ss Q3D (ug/mL)" = mouse_cavg_q3d,
                  "Mouse Cavg,ss Q4D (ug/mL)" = mouse_cavg_q4d,
                  "Published human PAD (mg/kg Q2W)" = human_pad,
                  "Human Cavg,ss at PAD (ug/mL)" = human_cavg_q2w),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Typical steady-state average concentrations behind the PAD projection."
)
# 5 mg/kg every 3 days in mice gives a Cavg near the 50 ug/mL threshold (Discussion).
stopifnot(abs(5 / (cl_mouse * 72) / 50 - 1) < 0.05)
```

Matching Cavg,ss with mice dosed every 3 days gives human Q2W doses of
`r sprintf("%.2f", pad$mouse_cavg_q3d[1] * cl_human * tau)` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", pad$mouse_cavg_q3d[2] * cl_human * tau)` mg/kg, within
about 10% of the published 1.8-7.0 mg/kg; the published range corresponds to
a mouse interval of about 66 h. The paper's printed mouse Cavg,ss (1.25 and
5.01 'mg/mL') and AUCss (420.0 and 1,683.4 'mg h/mL') values could not be
reproduced from Table 2 under any stated unit or interval (dose / CL alone
gives an AUC of 1,825 ug h/mL per 2.5 mg/kg dose), so they are not used as a
validation target.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV percentages.** Tables 1 and 2 report IIV as a percentage for
  exponential random effects without saying whether it is a CV or
  sqrt(omega^2) x 100. It is treated as a CV, omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1); at
  16-19% the two readings differ by under 2%, and at 43.4% (mouse CL) by about
  8% in variance. The assumed 30% human IIV is treated the same way.
* **Per-kg parameterisation.** The paper reports every parameter per kg body
  weight and doses in mg/kg; the models keep that form (dose in mg/kg to a
  nominal 1-kg subject) rather than introducing a body-weight covariate the
  authors did not use.
* **Human residual error and IIV** are the authors' assumed simulation values
  (Dirks and Meibohm 2010), encoded as fixed, not estimates.
* **Human values** use the per-kg numbers printed in Results (0.194, 47.2,
  0.44, 26.4); Equation 1 reproduces them to within 1%.
* **M3 / LLOQ.** The mouse fit used the M3 likelihood for BQL samples; that is
  an estimation feature and is not part of the simulation model.
* **Target-mediated disposition.** No TMDD was seen in healthy animals, which
  express little SIA-IgG; the authors note that tumour-bearing patients may
  show additional target-mediated clearance, which these models do not
  capture.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found (Europe PMC search,
  2026-11-17).
